title: Orthogonal bases from discrete weak cartesianness
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative nonarchimedean real absolute value. Assume its nonzero values are $\{\rho^m:m\in\mathbf Z\}$ for a real $\rho>1$. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and let $N:V\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ be a norm: $N(x)=0$ exactly when $x=0$, $N(x+y)\le\max(N(x),N(y))$, and $N(ax)=|a|N(x)$. Suppose $V$ has a basis $w_1,\ldots,w_r$ and real constants $c,C>0$ with $$c\max_i|a_i|\le N(\sum_i a_iw_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ Then $V$ has an orthogonal basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$: $$N(\sum_i a_iu_i)=\max_i|a_i|N(u_i)\qquad(a_i\in K).$$ For $V=0$ the basis is empty and the maximum is zero. Completeness of $K$ is not assumed.
